verdict.rationale: Meltano's docs say a project lives in a directory you create with `meltano init`, with pipelines declared as plugins in project config. They also say you can treat it like any other software project, with version control, code review and CI/CD. Portability is backed by documented project-specific Docker images and self-hosting on your own servers. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the git review and versioning workflow (community posts only call it open source, self-hosted and CLI-first).

support.subject: As a data engineer, my pipelines are plain code and config in my own repository — versioned, reviewed, and portable like any software

citations.quote: you can treat it like any other software development project and benefit from DataOps best practices such as version control, code review, and continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD)
Your project's plugins ... are defined under the plugins property, inside an array named after the plugin type (e.g. extractors, loaders).
Initialize a new project in a directory of your choosing using meltano init
you can greatly simplify this process ... by wrapping them all up into a project-specific Docker container image
You host and manage everything on your own servers
